clues.kinetics: Absorption is not influenced by food, and about 96% of the drug is bound to plasma protein. It is excreted in urine unchanged and extensively metabolized through CYP2D6 and CYP3A4.
clues.substance: A hydrochloride salt of molecular weight 415.96, soluble in water and in glacial acetic acid.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 5, 10 and 23 mg tablets, taken once daily.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated in hypersensitivity to the drug or to piperidine derivatives; nausea and diarrhea are the most common reasons for stopping.
clues.indication: Dementia of the Alzheimer type, across mild, moderate and severe disease.
clues.mechanism: A reversible inhibitor of acetylcholinesterase that raises acetylcholine levels, enhancing cholinergic function. There is no evidence it alters the course of the underlying dementia.

tell: A cholinesterase inhibitor with a half-life near 70 hours that accumulates 4- to 7-fold on once-daily dosing.
